findings: [P2] local_open.py: open_workspace trusts an unauthenticated /healthz response without checking that gui-server.lock is currently held. After the GUI exits, its metadata remains; another local OS user can bind the recorded port and return the predictable protocol/workspace response. aiops open then redirects the owner's browser, including the fresh ticket fragment, to attacker-controlled JavaScript. Removing the fragment in the legitimate frontend cannot protect this case. Verify live server ownership before issuing the ticket and bind ticket redemption to that server instance. Add a stale-lock/impersonated-health regression test.
